{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Primary endpoint lacks a stated analysis method",
      "quote": "The primary endpoint is ORR, defined as the proportion of subjects with a confirmed objective response of CR or PR based on Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors version 1.1 (RECIST v1.1).",
      "page": 46,
      "section": "2.2.1 Primary Endpoint",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The primary endpoint is defined but no statistical analysis method (e.g., exact binomial confidence interval, hypothesis test) is described in the statistical methods section.",
      "fix": "Add a description of the analysis for the primary endpoint, including the estimator, confidence interval method, and any hypothesis testing."
    },
    {
      "title": "Secondary endpoint 'Response in injected and noninjected target lesions' has no analysis",
      "quote": "Response in injected and noninjected target lesions per RECIST v1.1",
      "page": 46,
      "section": "2.2.2 Secondary Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "This secondary endpoint is listed but no corresponding analysis is described in the statistical methods section.",
      "fix": "Specify the analysis for this endpoint, including how response in injected vs noninjected lesions will be summarized and compared."
    },
    {
      "title": "Safety endpoint lacks a detailed analysis plan",
      "quote": "AEs, SAEs, and AEs leading to discontinuation or death, and severity of AEs as assessed by the National Cancer Institute Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events Version 5.0 (CTCAE v5.0)",
      "page": 46,
      "section": "2.2.2 Secondary Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The safety endpoint is defined but the statistical methods section only mentions that safety will be assessed; no specific analysis methods (e.g., incidence rates, severity grading summaries) are provided.",
      "fix": "Add a detailed safety analysis section describing how AEs will be summarized and analyzed."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing estimand attributes for primary endpoint",
      "quote": "ORR, defined as the proportion of subjects with a confirmed objective response of CR or PR based on RECIST v1.1.",
      "page": 46,
      "section": "2.2.1 Primary Endpoint",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The estimand for the primary endpoint is incomplete: the population (e.g., all treated subjects) is not explicitly stated, and intercurrent events (e.g., treatment discontinuation, death) and their handling are not defined.",
      "fix": "Define the estimand attributes: population, variable, intercurrent events strategy (e.g., treatment policy), and summary measure."
    },
    {
      "title": "No sample size justification provided",
      "quote": "The primary objective of this study is to determine the confirmed ORR with vidutolimod in combination with cemiplimab.",
      "page": 46,
      "section": "2.1.1 Primary Objective",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The protocol does not include a sample size section or any justification for the number of subjects, which is essential for a clinical trial.",
      "fix": "Add a sample size section with assumptions (e.g., expected ORR, precision, power) and the calculation method."
    },
    {
      "title": "No handling of missing data described",
      "quote": "Categorical variables will be summarized as the number and percentage of subjects within each category (with a category for missing data, if applicable).",
      "page": 91,
      "section": "8.3 General Considerations",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol only mentions including a missing category for categorical variables but does not describe how missing data will be handled in efficacy analyses (e.g., for ORR, PFS, OS).",
      "fix": "Add a section on missing data handling, specifying methods for each endpoint (e.g., censoring rules for time-to-event, sensitivity analyses)."
    },
    {
      "title": "No multiplicity adjustment described",
      "quote": "All efficacy endpoints will be summarized by cohort.",
      "page": 93,
      "section": "8.6 Efficacy Analyses",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol does not mention any adjustment for multiple comparisons across the multiple efficacy endpoints or cohorts, which may inflate the type I error.",
      "fix": "Describe the multiplicity strategy (e.g., hierarchical testing, Bonferroni) or justify why no adjustment is needed."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent analysis set for efficacy endpoints",
      "quote": "The Safety Analysis Set is defined as all subjects who receive at least 1 dose of study drug. This analysis set will be the primary analysis set for all efficacy and safety endpoints.",
      "page": 91,
      "section": "8.2 Analysis Sets",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Using the Safety Analysis Set for all efficacy endpoints is unusual and may not be appropriate for efficacy analyses; typically an intention-to-treat or per-protocol set is used. This could lead to bias.",
      "fix": "Define separate analysis sets for efficacy (e.g., full analysis set) and safety, and specify which set is primary for each endpoint."
    }
  ]
}
